newsitem.title: CANADA: Gulf Oil gets Arctic exploration license.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Oil gets Arctic exploration license.

text.p: Canadian Indian and Northern Affairs Minister Ronald Irwin on Tuesday said he would give two new oil and gas exploration licenses for the Northwest Territories to Gulf Canada Resources Ltd and Husky Oil Operations Ltd.
The licenses would entitle each company to drill one well in its allocated territory in the Mackenzie Delta region of the Northwest Territories during the nine-year life of each license.
Irwin's office said in a statement that the two licenses were granted in exchange for 21 former exploration permits for the Cape Bathurst region which lies east of the Mackenzie Delta.
Cape Bathurst is part of land that was given back to natives as part of a 1984 agreement between the Inuvialuit (Eskimos) and Ottawa.

"We have made the arrangement with the support of the Inuvialuit and the Government of the Northwest Territories, both of whom may benefit from renewed oil and gas exploration in the Mackenzie Delta," Irwin said in a press release.
